finding.text: The chat line's new `said_at` field is missing from the session-file schema: `ext/Session/doc/sessions.md:11` lists every field of an owner chat line and does not name `said_at`, or say that ordering reads `said_at ?? at` while ids stay `at`. Fix: add one line there that links to `ext/Chat/doc/notes.md#bubble-order`.

On reload, pieces inside one bubble are not ordered by `said_at`. `put_line` (`ext/Chat/Chat.js:697-701`) pushes a mergeable line onto the end of the last bubble and sets `last.dataset.at = at`, which can move backwards. So a slow send written after a later one still reads out of order within the bubble. Only `place()` orders, and it orders whole bubbles. Yet `notes.md:143` says "a reload keeps the order the owner spoke in". Fix: insert the piece by `at`, the way `speak` does, or narrow the doc's claim.

A fresh agent would read this task as unfixed. The task's landing `outcome` in `order/session.jsonl` still says "[ ] fix: not committed", and `order/report.md` ("The fix (short plan)") never says that steps 1–4 are now built (step 1 at ce1f45f58; steps 2–3 at 2cce08cea on `worktree/dictation-order-2`, not merged, Servex restart pending). Fix: update the outcome, and add a "Status" line to report.md.

Names don't match the code. `ux/Dictate/test/order.mjs:102` says `clock_offset`, and report.md and steps-2-3.md say `Session.clock_offset`, but the code exports `clock.offset` (`ext/Session/Session.js:93`). The test's header (`order.mjs:8-11`) still calls the third run "the KNOWN case … it waits for one clock" and in the same sentence says it now fails the run.

`order.mjs` doesn't test the `said_at` path. Its stubbed `say` (`order.mjs:35-39`) ignores `body.said_at`, and no run reloads the file, so step 3's "reload orders by said_at" is unproven. I re-ran it on the worktree (port 62998): all three runs `ok`, exit 0.

`clock.offset` stays 0 until the first `say` answer arrives. So the first sentence after a page load is stamped on the phone's clock, and if a resumed session's reply is already on screen, that first bubble can still jump above it. `session/new` and `resume` could seed the offset the same way.

`Session.say` is now `async` (`ext/Session/Session.js:79`), and Servex writes `said_at` only after a restart (`Servex/agents/Sessions.js:949`). Both are handled: the route passes the body straight through (`Sessions.js:1472`), and the client falls back to `at`. Merge and restart together.
